Subject. Dah Kwan News Agency - Application for re-registration -
News sheets for another week examined
Made by D.S.I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

On November 19, 1940, Liu Ya-hwa (協華),
editor, publisher and proprietor of the Dah Kwan News
Agency (大光通訊社), was called to and attended
Headquarters and informed of the instructions of P.A.
to A.C. (Special Branch) appended to attached report
of November 18 after he had been warned against the
use of objectionable phrases, such as appeared in
November 7, 11 and 12 issues of news sheets of his
agency. He promised to exercise greater care in
future.

News sheets for another week dated from
November 19 to 25, 1940, have been examined. However,
in the issue of November 21 was contained a report
"Observance of 'Anti-Air Raids' Day by Local Public
Bodies" which was deemed by the Police objectionable,
although it appeared in local newspapers on November
22 (see file N-267 attached), while the issue of
November 25 carried a report entitled "Authorities
Conduct Secret Investigations into the Activities
of Lawyers Following the Seizure of the 3rd Branch
of the Kiangsu High Court and the Shanghai 2nd Special
District Court" which was subject to deletion by
Police censors on November 26 when the Chinese-
American Daily News (中美日報) intended to include it
in its morning issue (see File N-267).

November 22, 1940. Morning Translation

Cheng Yien Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, National Herald,
Shun Pao and Sin Wan Pao :-

OBSERVANCE OF "ANTI-AIR RAIDS" DAY BY LOCAL PUBLIC BODIES

Yesterday, November 21, was fixed by the
National Government as the first "Anti-Air Raids" day.
The day was enthusiastically observed in
all parts of the country and exhibitions were held on anti-
air raid work. Consolation and relief were extended to those
people who had suffered from air raids. A movement was also
started for the collection of contributions to the anti-air
raids fund.

In view of the peculiar conditions prevailing
in Shanghai, no ceremony was held here in commemoration of the
day. The public, in recognition of the meritorious service
rendered by the air force during the past three years, made
voluntary contributions to the fund for the purchase of
aeroplanes to strengthen the air defence of the country.
Apart from the donation of $1,791 from the Lone Battalion,
local public bodies enthusiastically launched a movement to
secure donations for the purchase of aeroplanes. The public
also observed a short silence in memory of the officers and
men who had lost their lives in aerial combats and of all
people who were killed in air raids.

National Herald, Chinese-American Daily News, Cheng Yich Pao,
Sin Wan Pao :-

20,000 JAPANESE SOLDIERS CONCENTRATED AT WOOSUNG

According to information from reliable
sources, about 20,000 Japanese soldiers are now concentrated
at Woosung, Chang Hwa Pang and in the Woosung Forts. Most
of these men had arrived in transports last week from the
Upper Yangtse. Their worn and ragged uniforms indicate that
the men had been detached from the forces in various parts of
Central China.

It is generally believed that these men are
awaiting Japanese warships to transport them to Hainan Island
or Formosa to take part in Japan's southward expansion scheme.

Chinese-American Daily News, Cheng Yien Pao, Sin Wan Pao and
Shun Pao :-

THREE PERSONS ARRESTED IN SUN COMPANY'S TEA ROOM

According to information, the Settlement
Police arrested three male Chinese in the tea-room on the
fifth floor of the Sun Company off Yu Ya Ching Road at about
3.45 p.m. yesterday.
It was learned that these persons are
concerned in a certain case. They were removed to the
Police Station for further enquiries.

P. T. O.

1940年11月22日。晨間譯文

《誠言報》、《中美日報》、《國民新聞》、
《申報》及《新晚報》：-

本地公共團體紀念「防空」日

昨日，十一月二十一日，被國民政府定為首個「防空」日。
全國各地熱烈紀念這一日子，並舉行了防空工作展覽。向遭受空襲之苦的人民提供慰問和救濟。同時還發起了一項運動，為防空基金募集捐款。

鑑於上海 prevailing 的特殊情況，此地未舉行紀念儀式。公眾為表彰過去三年中空軍作出的功績，自願向購買飛機以加強國家空防的基金捐款。除孤軍捐贈1,791元外，本地公共團體還熱情發起運動以籌集購買飛機的捐款。公眾還短暫默哀，以紀念在空中戰鬥中犧牲的官兵以及所有在空襲中遇難的人們。

《國民新聞》、《中美日報》、《誠言報》、
《新晚報》：-

兩萬日軍聚集吳淞

據可靠消息來源稱，約兩萬名日軍現聚集於吳淞、張華浜及吳淞砲台。這些士兵大多於上週從長江上游乘運輸船抵達。他們破舊襤褸的制服表明，這些人是從華中各地部隊中調離出來的。

人們普遍認為，這些人正在等待日本軍艦將他們運往海南島或台灣，以參與日本的南進計劃。

《中美日報》、《誠言報》、《新晚報》及
《申報》：-

三人被捕於先施公司茶室

據悉，租界警察於昨日下午約3時45分，在虞洽卿路旁先施公司五樓的茶室逮捕了三名中國男子。
獲悉這些人涉及某一案件。他們已被帶往警察局進行進一步訊問。

November 22, 1940. Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News, Cheng Yien Pao, Sin Wan Pao,
Shun Pao, National Herald :-

ATTEMPTED ASSASSINATION AT A MARRIAGE PARTY ON FOOCHOW ROAD

At 7 p.m. yesterday, an attempt was made on
the lives of a bridegroom and a bride at the Dah San Sin
Restaurant (大三仙菜館) 679 Foochow Road.
Loo Ting (盧鼎), age 21, native of Changshu,
son of a principal shareholder in the Li Wei Loo Club
(利威廬俱樂部) on Yu Yuen Road (formerly known as the Hollywood
Garden 好萊塢樂園), was married to Miss Sung Chuen-ying
(宋春英) yesterday. After the wedding ceremony, which
took place in the hall of the restaurant on the ground floor,
the bridegroom and bride left the hall to go to a room
on the upper floor for a rest. It was just 7 p.m. As
the couple were walking on the stairs, three men, two of
whom were armed with pistols, suddenly entered the restaurant
and fired four shots at them. One bullet hit the staircase,
two others struck a counter and a fourth smashed a large
glass on the wall. Both the bridegroom and the bride were
uninjured, but became panic-stricken and sought shelter in
the halls. Great disorder prevailed and the guests were
terror-stricken. After firing another shot as a
demonstration at the entrance of the restaurant, the gunmen
disappeared.
Upon hearing the pistol shots, a C.P.C. on
duty in front of the Tien Zay Wu Tan Theatre (天蟾舞臺)
near the restaurant came up and fired three shots at the
escaping gunmen, one of whom fired a shot in return. Nobody
was hit in the exchange of shots. The gunmen made good
their escape in the crowd. A private ricksha coolie named
Chen Chin-sun (陳金生) in the employ of the Fong Wong
Girl Guide Establishment (鳳凰女子指導處) of No. 8 Fah Ziang
Li (法祥里), Yunnan Road, was injured in the right
shoulder and was removed to the Lester Chinese Hospital,
where he succumbed through loss of blood.
Upon receipt of a report, a large party of
detectives and policemen were detailed to the spot to make
an investigation. Five empty cartridge cases were found
in the Dah San Sin Restaurant. The bridegroom, the bride,
and the accountants and waiters of the restaurant were
taken to the Police Station for interrogation.
According to information secured by our
reporter, the bridegroom Loo Ting is the son of a gambling
den owner and is the owner of the Van Li Rice Shop (萬利米店)
on Feng Zin Road (方浜路), Nantao.

Chinese-American Daily News :-

"TELEPHONE IN LAWYERS' ROOM IN SECOND SPECIAL DISTRICT
COURT REMOVED; FIRST SPECIAL DISTRICT COURT REFUSES
TO ACCEPT ILLEGAL COURT DOCUMENTS."

The Shanghai Second Special District Court
recently changed its attitude and most of the lawyers are
now unwilling to attend its sessions. The telephone
installed in the lawyers' room of the Court was removed
on the morning of November 21.

《中美日報》、《誠言報》、《新晚報》、
《申報》、《國民新聞》：-

福州路婚宴上的刺殺未遂事件

昨晚7時，福州路679號大三仙菜館發生了一起針對新郎和新娘的刺殺未遂事件。
盧鼎（Loo Ting），21歲，常熟人，是愚園路利威廬俱樂部（前稱好萊塢樂園）主要股東之子，昨日與宋春英小姐（Miss Sung Chuen-ying）結婚。婚禮在一樓大廳舉行後，新郎新娘離開大廳前往樓上房間休息。當時正好是晚上7點。當這對夫婦走在樓梯上時，三名男子突然進入餐廳，其中兩人手持手槍，向他們開了四槍。一顆子彈擊中樓梯，另外兩顆擊中櫃檯，第四顆擊碎了牆上的一大塊玻璃。新郎和新娘均未受傷，但驚慌失措，躲進大廳。現場一片混亂，賓客們驚恐萬狀。槍手在餐廳門口又開了一槍示警後消失。
聽到槍聲後，在附近天蟾舞臺執勤的一名中央捕房警員趕來，向逃竄的槍手開了三次槍，其中一名槍手還擊一槍。交火中無人受傷。槍手混入人群中成功逃脫。雲南路法祥里8號鳳凰女子指導處僱用的一名私人黃包車夫陳金生（Chen Chin-sun）右肩受傷，被送往雷士德華人醫院，因失血過多死亡。
接到報告後，大批偵探和警察被派往現場進行調查。在大三仙菜館發現了五個空彈殼。新郎、新娘以及餐廳的會計和服務員被帶到警察局接受訊問。
據本報記者獲得的消息，新郎盧鼎是一名賭場老闆的兒子，也是南市方浜路萬利米店的老闆。

《中美日報》：-

Forwarded herewith is an application for

Agency (大光通訊社), with an office in Room 221 House

Zau Ya-hwa, native of Ningpo, aged 23, claims

assumed name of Zau Shu-yah (邹建白), former

now defunct Dah Kung News Agency (大公社), then
located in Kiukiang Road, but left it in August 1938
when he joined the Dah Kwan News Agency and occupied

editor, publisher and proprietor of the news agency
(see attached translation of letter dated 30.7.40.)

Headquarters and told to come to this office again
together with Wong Sih-zung, with a view to ascertaining

Letter from the Dah Kwan News Agency to the Special
Branch of the Shanghai Municipal Police:-

March 16, 1940.

To the Deputy Commissioner of the Special Branch of
the Shanghai Municipal Police,

This news agency was registered with the Special
Branch in October, 1938, and Registration Certificate
No. 315 was issued. Ever since it began distributing
news sheets, it has been carrying on according to the
instructions of your Branch and has been careful in its
work. Copies of the news sheets have been submitted
every day for your examination.

Recently, owing to negligence on the part of the
employees of this agency, it distributed news contravening
the instructions of your Branch and has thus been ordered
to cease functioning. Acting on your instructions, this
agency has suspended distributing news sheets with effect
from March 14.

As it is the first offence, we ask you for pardon
and for permission to resume operations. Hereafter, we will
be especially careful and will never repeat the offence.

We hereby write you this letter begging you to grant
our request. A reply will be much appreciated.

The Dah Kwan News Agency
( 大光社 ), Shanghai.

致上海公共租界工部局警务处特务科副警务处长，

本社于1938年10月在特务科注册，并发给第315号注册证书。自开始分发新闻稿以来，本社一直按照贵科的指示开展工作，谨慎行事。新闻稿副本每日提交供贵科审查。

鉴于这是初犯，恳请贵科宽恕并允许恢复运作。今后，我们将格外小心，绝不再犯。

March 14, 1940. Morning Translations.

Chinese-American Daily News :-

ACTIVITIES OF PRESS GANG IN HONGKEW : COOLIES CONSCRIPTED

The Dah Kwang News Agency (大光社) has secured
the following information :-
Since the Japanese authorities announced the
re-opening of Hongkew and authorized Chinese to enter the
area without passes, cases of conscription of Chinese have
occurred in the Eastern District and vicinity. Local
residents have become alarmed and dare not visit Hongkew.
According to information secured, the press
gang was again active yesterday in the Eastern District
of Hongkew. The work is undertaken by Formosans and
Koreans wearing a band of white cloth on their arms.
They forcibly take away Chinese of the labouring class
and send them to various places to work as road construction
coolies. On March 13, many Chinese coolies were conscripted
on East Yuhang Road, Alcock Road and Kwenming Road.

1940年3月14日。上午译文。

《中美日报》：-

虹口抓伕队活动：强征苦力

大光社（大光社）获得如下信息：-
自从日本当局宣布重新开放虹口并允许中国人无需通行证进入该地区以来，东区及周边地区发生了强征中国人的案件。当地居民感到恐慌，不敢前往虹口。据 obtained 的信息，昨天抓伕队在虹口东区再次活跃。这项工作由手臂上佩戴白布带的台湾人和朝鲜人执行。他们强行带走劳工阶层的中国人，并将他们送到各处充当修路苦力。3月13日，许多中国苦力在东余杭路、阿尔科克路（Alcock Road）和昆山路（Kwenming Road）被强征。

March 9, 1940.
Morning Translation.

MAINICHI

DAH KWAN NEWS AGENCY RESPONSIBLE FOR WILD RUMOURS
OF ABDUCTION OF CHINESE BY JAPANESE

Groundless rumours that Chinese
were being abducted by Japanese in Hongkew and Yangtsepoo
areas have been spread by Chinese newspapers published in
the Settlement to the south of the Soochow Creek. This
wild rumour has been circulated in a systematic manner.
A certain Hoh (何) of the Dah
Kwan News Agency, who is concurrently a member of the
Three Principles of the People Young Men's Association,
is responsible for the circulation of the rumour. When
Hongkow area was re-opened, the news agency mobilized the
members of the propaganda department of the Young Men's
Association and sent Zau Tsung-faung (趙春芳) and Chen
Chao (陳超), ex-deputy foreman in the Mohino Department
of the Ewo Cotton Spinning Mill, and three other men to
Hongkew area to spread the rumour among Chinese workers
and pedlars in tea shops and markets.
It is said that Zau Tsung-faung
is in the habit of meeting his members every night in a
tea shop on Nanking Road.

大光通訊社对日本人绑架中国人的荒谬谣言负责

苏州河南岸租界内出版的中文报纸散布了关于日本人在虹口和杨浦区绑架中国人的毫无根据的谣言。这一荒谬谣言以系统化的方式传播。
大光通訊社的一名何姓（Hoh）人员，同时也是三民主义青年团成员，对该谣言的传播负有责任。当虹口地区重新开放时，该通讯社动员了青年团宣传部的成员，并派遣赵春芳（Zau Tsung-faung，音译）和陈超（Chen Chao，音译，怡和纱厂 Mohino 部门前副工头）以及另外三人前往虹口地区，在茶馆和市场中向中国工人和小贩散布谣言。

Date October 21, 1938.

Subject Dah Kwan News Agency.

Made by T.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

Discreet enquiries have failed to locate any person bearing the name Zau Laung-loo (邵夢廬), who is alleged to be the publisher of the newly formed Dah Kwan (大光) News Agency, or to establish definitely that Zau Laung-loo and Zau Shu-pah (邵虛白), committee member of the defunct General Labour Union, and editor of the defunct Dah Kung News Agency, is one and the same person.

Nevertheless, in Room 606, Pootung Guild Building, 1454 Avenue Edward VII, where the office of the Dah Kwan News Agency will be located, there is already established, a news agency known as Modern News Agency (現代通信社), the chief editor of which is the same Wong Sih-sung (王雪塵) as that mentioned in the attached application as proprietor of the new organization.

It is said that through the medium of the Modern News Agency, Zau Shu-pah has already been supplying news articles to local Chinese press. There is reason to believe that for the sake of convenience, Zau Shu-pah is preparing to resuscitate the defunct Dah Kung News Agency under the title of the Dah Kwan News Agency, and assumes the fictitious name Zau Maung-loo in order to camouflage his past activities. It is quite possible that Zau Shu-pah, one of the prominent members of the General Labour Union which was under Kuomintang influence, who is in Shanghai, but keeps his movements secret, may arrange to have someone to pose as Zau Maung-loo, if necessary.

297

Sih Tse liang
C. D. I.
